slot.brief: Soap bubble of given radius and surface tension; find the excess pressure inside using 4S/r; diagram can show the bubble with inner/outer radii.

stem: A soap bubble has radius $4.0$ cm and an excess pressure of $3.0$ Pa. As shown in the figure, determine the surface tension of the soap solution.

verdicts.working: For a soap bubble, ΔP = 4T/R. Thus T = (3.0 Pa)(0.040 m)/4 = 0.030 N m⁻¹.

working:
$P_i-P_o=\dfrac{4S}{R}$
$S=\dfrac{(3.0)(0.040)}{4}=0.030$ N m$^{-1}$

Independent check: For a soap bubble, ΔP = 4T/R. Thus T = (3.0 Pa)(0.040 m)/4 = 0.030 N m⁻¹.
solution:
For a soap bubble, the excess pressure is $\Delta P=\dfrac{4S}{R}$.
$$S=\frac{\Delta P\,R}{4}=\frac{(3.0)(0.040)}{4}=0.030\ \text{N m}^{-1}$$

draft.stem: A soap bubble has radius $4.0$ cm and an excess pressure of $3.0$ Pa. As shown in the figure, determine the surface tension of the soap solution.

figure.description: Draw a circular cross-section of a thin spherical soap bubble as two closely spaced concentric circles. Label the region inside the inner circle $P_i$ and the region outside the outer circle $P_o$. Draw a straight radial line from the centre to the middle of the film and label it $R = 4.0$ cm. Add a note beside the bubble: $P_i - P_o = 3.0$ Pa. Do not include surface tension or any equation.

draft.distractor_notes: A: Uses an extra factor of 2 in the denominator. C: Uses the liquid-drop formula $2S/R$. D: Uses $S=(P_i-P_o)R$, omitting the factor of 4.
